title: Proof of Life, Suspension and Held Payment Figures — Income Annuities
content:
Income Annuities payments depend on the annuitant being alive and on payments reaching the payee. The figures below set when a certificate of existence is required, how long suspensions run before a record must clear them, and how held payments are treated. They are the same on all six tiers: Ashgrove Income Annuity Life Only, Cash Refund, 10-Year Certain, 20-Year Certain, Joint 50% Survivor and Joint 100% Survivor.

| Figure | Value on every tier |
|---|---|
| Annuitant age from which an annual certificate of existence is required | 90 |
| Interval between required certificates of existence | 12 months |
| Period after a certificate of existence is requested within which it must be returned before payments are suspended | 60 calendar days |
| Whether payments held during a suspension earn interest when released | No |
| How a payment returned undeliverable is reissued once instructions are confirmed | By check |
| Period within which an unverified report of death must be confirmed by a certified death certificate before payments resume | 30 calendar days |
| Time after a suspension is cleared within which the held payments are released in one sum | 5 business days |

### Questions the figures answer

**From what age is a certificate of existence asked for?** From an annuitant's attained age of 90, every 12 months.

**How long does the annuitant have to return a requested certificate?** 60 calendar days from the request.

**Do held installments grow while held?** No — the figure for interest on suspended payments is "no" on every tier.

**In what form is a returned payment sent again?** By check, once instructions are confirmed.

**How quickly are held installments paid once a suspension is cleared?** In one sum within 5 business days.

**What period applies to an unconfirmed report of death?** 30 calendar days for confirmation by a certified death certificate.
